chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Studio session length and ease of cutting four sides
summary: Sessions ran about three hours and top musicians could do four sides easily.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Okay. How about -- Oh. Just in talking about recording, was their a set time that you had to make recordings? I mean, if you went in to make a recording at one o'clock in the afternoon did you have to be finished by five, six?
Were there any -- what kind of existed in studios constraints, if any, (inaudible)?

Well we never had any strains on us. We had a recording date -- Most of the time that we was recording, like ten o'clock or eleven o'clock -- whatever time we set -- most of the -- It was a usual thing, three hour day like they have now. You know, a session of three hours -- whatever the union call for. It was for three hours.
With good musicians, you could do several selections in that time?
Oh, we could do anything you want (inaudible). Yeah, We could do four sides
